2. Geological Setting andSampling
2.1. Xilinhot–SongliaoBlock
TheXSBislocatedonthenorthsideoftheSLS(Figure1b).Wecarriedoutnewpaleomagneticinvestigations
tothesoutheastofXilinhotCity,easternInnerMongolia.Inthisregion,PaleoproterozoicandOrdovician
metamorphic rocks (e.g., Baoyintu Group and Baoerhantu Group; Figure 2; Bureau of Geology Mineral
Resources of Inner Mongol Autonomous Region (BGMRIM), 1991; China University of Geosciences,
Wuhan(CUGW),2009;Geetal.,2011;Hao&Xu,1997;Liuetal.,2017;Xuetal.,2015;Zhaoetal.,2016)
areconsideredtobethebasementandareunconformablyoverlainbythickPaleozoicandMesozoicsedi-
mentarysuccessions(Figure2;BGMRIM,1991;Hanetal.,2017;Liuetal.,2017;Xuetal.,2015).
TheMiddlePermianZhesiFmiswidelyexposedintheXilinhotarea.Thesedimentaryrocksofthisforma-
tionare~397–806mthickandcomposedmainlyofgrayish‐greensandstone–conglomerateinthelowermost
member,siltstonesandsandstonesinterbeddedwithgraybioclasticlimestonesinthemiddlemember,and
redbedsinterbeddedwithtuffsandtuffaceoussandstonesintheuppermember(Figure2;BGMRIM,1991;
CUGW, 2009). The Zhesi Fm is a shallow marine clastic succession that is likely Wordian in age
(CUGW,2009;Shenetal.,2006;Yangetal.,2017),basedonconodonts(e.g.,Mesogondolellaneoprolongata),
fusulinids (e.g., Pseudodoliolina ozawai), corals (e.g., Lophophyllidium pendulum), and brachiopods (e.g.,
Yakovleviamammatiformis).ThisformationisconformablyoverlainbytheUpperPermianLinxiFmand
conformably or disconformably overlies the Lower Permian Dashizhai Fm (Figure 2; BGMRIM, 1991;
CUGW, 2009). The Linxi Fm and Dashizhai Fm yield LA–ICP–MS zircon U–Pb ages of 252.6 ± 1.7 to
248.4 ± 4.8 Ma for volcano‐sedimentary rocks (Bian et al., 2013; Zheng et al., 2014) and at 279 ± 3 to
287.5±1.4Maforvolcanicrocks,respectively(Figure2;Zhangetal.,2008,2016).DetritalzirconU–Pbages
obtainedfromZhesiFmclasticrocksintheXilinhot–HexigtenBannerareahaveayoungestagepeakat
~268Ma(Eizenhöferetal.,2014).AtuffbednearthetopoftheZhesiFminthewesternHexigtenBanner
areayieldsaLA–ICP–MSzirconU–Pbageof262±1Ma(Lietal.,2018).Thus,theZhesiFmsedimentary
rockswerelikelydepositedduringtheWordian–Capitanian(~268–262Ma).
InDalainuoerTowntothesoutheastofXilinhotCity,wecollected119redbedsamplesfrom14sitesinthe
uppermemberoftheZhesiFm(Figure3).Inaddition,onesampleoftuff(18DN01)wascollectedfromthe
paleomagnetic sampling section for zircon U–Pb age dating (Figures 3 and 4c). Hand specimen and
thin‐sectionphotographsofthetuffsampleareshowninFigureS1inthesupportinginformation.Theregio-
nalunconformitiesneartheXilinhotareaoccurbetweentheUpperPermianLinxiFmtotheLowerJurassic
HongqiFm(BGMRIM,1991;CUGW,2009),suggestingthattheearliestfoldingandregionaldeformationof
ZhesiFmstratatookplacefromtheLatePermiantotheEarlyJurassic.
2.2. NorthernMarginoftheNCB
OnthesouthsideoftheSLS,wecarriedoutpaleomagneticsamplingneareasternChifengcity(Figure1b).
ThisregionislocatedatthenorthernmarginoftheNCB,whereArcheantoPaleoproterozoicmetamorphic
rocks comprise the basement, covered by thick Paleozoic marine and terrestrial sedimentary successions
that,inturn,areoverlainunconformablybyMesozoicandCenozoicterrestrialvolcanicandclasticstrata
(Figure2;BGMRIM,1991;Zhangetal.,2016).PermianvolcanicrocksarewidelyexposedintheChifeng
area. The volcanic strata are ~800 m thick and composed mainly of andesitic lava with interbedded
volcano‐clasticrocks(Figure2;BGMRIM,1991;Zhang,Zhao,etal.,2016).Theyareunconformablyoverlain
by Jurassic–Cretaceous volcano‐sedimentary rocks, and conformably or disconformably overlie the
Carboniferous–Permian marine sedimentary rocks (Figure 2; BGMRIM, 1991). Early geological mapping
placedthesevolcanicrocksintheLowerPermianQingfengshanFm(BGMRIM,1991).However,recentzir-
conU–Pbdatingindicatesthattheeruptionofvolcanicrockslastedfor~20MyrduringthePermian,from
273±6Mato255.5±2.5Ma(Figure2;Xuetal.,2016;Zhang,Zhao,etal.,2016).
Inthisstudy,atotalof127individualorientedandesiteandsandstonesamplesfrom14siteswerecollected
fromthetopoftheQingfengshanFmnearTanjiagouandAohanqi.Theseincludeatleast10interbedded
lava flows which span sufficient time to likely average out paleogeomagnetic secular variation. The

More than 1,000 representative zircon grains were handpicked under a binocular microscope from each
sample. They, together with zircon standards, were mounted in transparent epoxy‐resin and polished to
exposecrystalinteriors.Zirconsweredocumentedwithtransmittedandreflectedlightphotomicrographs
and cathodoluminescence (CL) images to study their internal structures and find suitable locations for
analyses.
The U, Th, and Pb isotope compositions were measured using laser ablation multicollector inductively
coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA–MC–ICP–MS) at the Mineral Laser Microprobe Analysis

3.2. U–PbDatingResults
3.2.1. ZhesiFm
Sample18DN01,agraytuff,wascollectedfromDalainuoerTown(Figure3c;43.379°N,116.918°E).More
than 1,000 zircons were separated from this sample, including some inherited zircons; 40 were used for
U–Pb isotopic dating. These zircons are typically 50–150 μm long and 30–80 μm wide (Figure 5a).
Thirty‐eight zircon analyses with discordance ≤10% yield two populations of 206Pb/238U ages at 268–264

Oursamplingsectionwas98mthickandcontainsredconglomerates,sandstones,andsiltstones,represent-

the sampling section. We therefore conclude that our sampling section was deposited during ~265.8–

3.2.2. QingfengshanFm
Andesitesamples16TJ01and17TJ01werecollectedfromthetopoftheQingfengshanFmnearTanjiagou,
Aohanqi(Figure3d;42.470°N,119.920°).Thezirconcrystalsareeuhedraltosubhedral,70–150μmlongand
30–60μmwide,anddisplayedfine‐scaleoscillatoryzoning(Figures5dand5g),indicatingamagmaticori-
gin.Thirtyanalysesofzirconsfrom16TJ01and28analysesofzirconsfrom17TJ01areconcordant(i.e.,dis-
cordance ≤10%) and yield age populations of 260–251 and 260–254 Ma, respectively (Table S1).
Weighted‐mean 206Pb/238U ages are 254.8 ± 1.2 Ma (N = 30, MSWD = 0.66; Figure 5) and 257.1 ± 1.4
(N = 28; MSWD = 0.19; Figure 5), respectively. Therefore, the andesites at the top of the Qingfengshan
Fmwereeruptedat~255Ma.
4. Paleomagnetic Laboratory Techniques andMeasurements
Coresamplesof2.5cmindiameterwerecutinto2.2‐cm‐longspecimens.Allpaleomagneticspecimenswere
measuredatthePaleomagnetismandEnvironmentalMagnetismLaboratoryoftheCUGB,China.Toiden-
tify magnetic minerals and select appropriate demagnetization methods and steps, isothermal remanent
magnetization(IRM),back‐fielddemagnetizationofsaturationIRM(SIRM),andthermaldemagnetization
ofthree‐axisIRMs(Lowrie,1990)weremeasuredforrepresentativespecimens.Fieldsof2.4T,0.4T,and
0.12TwereappliedusingtheIM10–30pulsemagnetizeralongthez‐,y‐,andx‐axesofthespecimensinturn,
followedbystepwisethermaldemagnetizationupto680°C.IRMwasmeasuredusingaJR‐6Aspinnermag-
netometer.Finally,basedontherockmagneticanalyses,allspecimensweresubjectedtostepwisethermal
demagnetization using an ASC TD–48 oven (residual magnetic field <10 nT). Remanent magnetizations
weremeasuredusinga2G755‐to4‐Kcryogenicmagnetometer.Allthermaldemagnetizationandrema-
nence measurements were performed within a shielded room at CUGB with residual fields of <200 nT.
Remanentmagnetizationdirectionsofallspecimenswereisolatedbyusingprincipalcomponentanalysis
(Kirschvink, 1980). The average paleomagnetic directions were calculated using Fisherian statistics
(Fisher, 1953). The computer softwarepackages developed by Cogné(2003) andEnkin (1990) wereused
toprocessandanalyzethepaleomagneticdata.
5. Rock‐Magnetic Results
FortheredbedspecimensoftheZhesiFm,theIRMacquisitioncurveshowsaslowincreaseanddoesnot
reachsaturationat2.4T,andprogressiveback‐fielddemagnetizationofSIRMindicatesthatthecoercivity
of remanence is ~600 mT (Figure 6a). Coercivity spectra analysis (Kruiver et al., 2001) shows that the
low‐coercivity component constitutes ∼10% of the SIRM and the high‐coercivity component constitutes
∼90%(Figures6band6c),suggestingthathigh‐coercivitymagneticcarriersaredominant.Stepwisethermal
demagnetization of three orthogonal IRM components (Lowrie, 1990) shows that the IRM intensity was
dominantbythehard(2.4T)andintermediate(0.4T)componentsandthattheirIRMintensitiesrapidly
decreasearound675°C(Figure6d).Thus,theserock‐magneticresultsrevealthathematiteisthepredomi-
nantmagneticcarrierintheredbedsoftheZhesiFm.
FortheandesiteandsandstonespecimensfromsitesTJ1toTJ9oftheQingfengshanFm,theIRMacquisi-

combined with the finding that the coercivity of remanence is <50 mT (Figure 6e), indicates that
low‐coercivity magnetic carriers are dominant. The coercivity spectra analysis reveals two low‐coercivity

6. Petrographic Results
TocheckwhetherthemainmagneticcarriersoftheZhesiFmredbedsandQingfengshanFmandesiticlavas
preserveprimarymicrotextures,weperformedadetailedmicroscopicexaminationofrepresentativespeci-
mensusingaZeissSUPPA55fieldemissionscanningelectronmicroscope(SEM)underanacceleratingvol-
tageof20kVandaworkingdistanceof15.9mmattheFieldEmissionSEMLaboratory,CUGB.Toensure
high‐qualityimaging,thepolishedspecimenswerecoatedwithplatinumbeforeanalysis.Energydispersive
spectrometry(EDS)analysiswasusedtoobtainelementalcompositions.
SEM observations and EDS analysis confirmed that the main magnetic carriers are Fe‐oxides (Figure 7).
MostFe‐oxidesshoweuhedraltoirregularshapesandvariablesizes,rangingmainlyfromafewmicrons
toseveralhundredsofnanometers(Figure7).FortheZhesiFmredbeds,nopigmentarycharacteristicfor
hematitewasfoundundermicroscopicexamination(Figures7aand7b),whichmayindicatethepresence
ofinitialdetritalironphases.FortheQingfengshanFmandesiticlavas,theFe‐oxidegrainsshownoobvious
oxidizedrimsinBSE images(Figures7c and7d),suggestingthat theywereformedbyhigh‐temperature
exsolution during initial cooling, rather than by the long‐term low‐temperature oxidation of original
Fe‐oxidesaftercooling.
7. Paleomagnetic Results
7.1. MiddlePermianZhesiFm
Ofthe119specimensfromtheZhesiFmredbedsthatunderwentstepwisethermaldemagnetization,105
specimensyieldedusefulmagneticsignals(Table1).Thenaturalremanentmagnetization(NRM)intensities
ranged from 1 to 200 mA/m. Representative Zijderveld plots (after Zijderveld, 1967) are shown in
Figures 8a–8f. A low‐temperature component (LTC) could be defined for most specimens between room
temperature and 300°C. The in situ LTCs are clustered around the local recent geomagnetic field (RGF)
direction(D=0°,I=62.1°,calculatedbasedonthegeocentricaxialdipole[GAD]model,FigureS2a),which
revealsthattheLTCrepresentsaviscousremanentmagnetization(VRM)oftheRGF.Asmallnumberof
specimensalsoincludedanunstablemoderate‐temperaturecomponent(MTC)between450°Cand520°C
(e.g.,Figure8d).AfterremovaloftheLTCandMTC,astablehigh‐temperaturecomponent(HTC)decayed
toward the origin near the unblocking temperature of 680°C. All HTC‐bearing sites display a uniformly
reversedpolarity,pointingsoutheastandupaftertiltcorrection(Figure10;Table1).Thesite‐meandirection
for14sitesisDg=154.9°,Ig=27.8°,k=15.8,andα =10.3°insitu,whichissignificantlydifferentfromthe
95
modernfielddirection,andDs=156.4°,Is=−18.0°,k=84.0,andα =4.4°aftertiltcorrection(Figure10;
95
Table1).Althoughthesedirectionsshowauniformlyreversedpolaritybecausetheirremanentmagnetiza-
tions were acquired in the late Wordian (~265 Ma, for discussion, see section 3.2.1) during the Reversed
Subchron GU1r (~265.8–264.4 Ma; Hounslow & Balabanov, 2016), they could pass a fold test
(McElhinny,1964;McFadden,1990)at95%and99%confidencelevelsandthevalueoftheprecisionpara-
meter “k” reaches a maximum at 110% unfolding in the stepwise unfolding test (Figure S3a; Watson &
Enkin, 1993). The prefolding origin of the HTC indicates that it was acquired before the Early Jurassic.
Furthermore, the paleopole of the Zhesi Fm is significantly different from the Late Permian to Early
Triassic poles (Table 2). We therefore consider the HTC to be a primary magnetization. Using the
N‐dependent A envelope proposed by Deenen et al. (2011, 2014), we expect our data to fit the

A =4.37°andA =1.87°reliabilityenvelopefor105specimens,whichcanbeappliedasacriterion

After removal of the LTC, a stable HTC decayed toward the origin near the unblocking temperatures of
580°C(sitesTJ1–TJ9)or680°C(sitesTJ10–14).TheHTChasdual‐polaritydirections,withmagnetization
directed northwestward and moderately down as normal polarity and southeastward and moderately up
as reversed polarity (Figure 11). The in situ site‐mean direction for 14 sites is Dg = 313.1°, Ig = −58.3°,
k = 28.9, and α = 7.5°, which is significantly different from the modern field direction, and
95
Ds = 139.3°, Is = −47.1°, k = 189.9, and α = 2.9° after tilt correction (Figure 11; Table 1). All of the
95
HTCs pass the fold tests of McElhinny (1964) and McFadden (1990) at the 95% and 99% confidence
levels (Table 1), and the value of the precision parameter “k” reaches a maximum at 117% unfolding in
the stepwise unfolding test (Figure S3b; Watson & Enkin, 1993), indicating that the HTC was acquired
before tilting. The dual polarity directions correspond to the two adjacent polarity zones (Figure 2;
LP1r and LP2n) and pass a reversal test (McFadden & McElhinny, 1990) at the 95% confidence level
(class B) with an angle between the two averages γ = 4.4 < γ = 6.3. Thus, the HTC is
o critical
interpreted as a primary magnetization.

8. Discussion
8.1. AnalysisofthePermianPaleomagneticPoles
ThePermianpaleomagneticdatafromtheXSBandNCBwereappraisedbyapplyingthe7‐pointdataquality
criterionsystem(VanderVoo,1990),andtheresultsarecompiledinTable2withacutoffofQ≥4.Inthe
supportinginformationwepresentredefinedagesforallthestratasampledforpaleomagnetism(TextS1),
basedonthecompiledbiostratigraphicandisotopicagedata.

8.2. ImplicationsforPaleogeographicEvolution
TodeterminetheoriginoftheSLSandthepaleogeographicevolutionoftheEastAsianblocks(i.e.,NCB,
SCB,XSB,MOB,andJiamusi–BureyaBlock),weproposeanewreconstruction modelforthe265to246
Ma interval based on current paleomagnetic, paleontological, and geological evidence (Figure 13). Our
new subduction–collision model differs from that of previous studies (Domeier & Torsvik, 2014; Huang
etal.,2018;Zhangetal.,2018)byapplyingtighterkinematicconstraintstotheclosureofthePAObasin.
During the Middle Permian (~265 Ma), the paleolatitude difference between the XSB and the NCB was
5.3°±7.2°(Figure12b).Althoughthisdifferencedoesnotequalthewidthoftheinterveningoceanbasin,
we can conclude that there has been 580 ± 790 km of lithospheric shortening between the XSB and the
NCBsince~265Ma.Geologicalevidencesuggeststhat(1)theMiddlePermianmarinetoshallow‐marine
strata(ZhesiFmorHuanggangliangFm)areextensivelydistributedonbothsidesoftheSLS,asfurthersup-
portedbythefossilrecord(BGMRIM,1991;Eizenhöfer&Zhao,2018;Shenetal.,2006;Shi,2006;Wang

etal.,2004;Wang&Zhang,2003);(2)subduction‐relatedmagmatismisrecordedonbothsidesoftheSLS
(Eizenhöfer & Zhao, 2018; Zhang, Zhao, et al., 2016); and (3) ophiolite complexes have been identified
within the SLS, yielding zircon U–Pb ages of ~256–250 Ma (Jian et al., 2010; Miao et al., 2008, 2007).
Therefore,aresidualoceanbasin(thePAOorSolonkerOcean)mighthaveexistedbetweentheXSBand
theNCBat~265Ma(Figure13a).However,duetothescarcityofpre‐Permianpaleomagneticdatafrom
the MOB, XSB and NCB, the question remains as to whether the ocean was long‐lived (e.g., Liu
etal.,2017;Xiaoetal.,2018)orwasreopened(e.g.,Songetal.,2015;Xuetal.,2018)beforethePermian.
During the Middle Permian, terrestrial floras were different on either side of the SLS, as this residual
ocean basin was a geographic barrier. The northern side of this suture (i.e., XSB, MOB, Tarim, and
Siberia) was characterized by a temperate Angara flora, whereas the southern side (i.e., NCB and SCB)
was characterized by a tropical–subtropical Cathaysia Flora (Figure 13a; Deng et al., 2009;
Huang, 1980, 1993; Shen, Du, et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2016). As the PAO was a small ocean basin
(<550kmwide)betweentheXSBandtheNCB,marinefauna(e.g.,Zhesibrachiopods)wasfreetomingle
(Figure 13a; Deng et al., 2009; Shen et al., 2006; Shi, 2006), which was encouraged by the influence of
south‐flowing cold‐water currents from the Mongol–Okhotsk Ocean in the north, and north‐flowing
warm‐water paleoequatorial currents from the Paleo‐Pacific Ocean in the south (Figure 13a; Shi, 2006;
Yang & Xia, 2004). Because the XSB and the NCB were located within the 10°–20°N tropical zone and
were surrounded by ocean basins (Figure 13a; i.e., Paleo‐Tethys Ocean, Paleo‐Pacific Ocean, PAO, and
the small ocean between the XSB and JB), some blocks (e.g., XSB, NCB and South China) of the East
AsiandomainhadahumidenvironmentthatwasconducivetothegrowthoftropicalCathaysiaFloraon
thesouthernsideoftheSLSduringtheMiddlePermian(Sun,1999,2006).
From265to255Ma,boththeXSBandtheNCBdriftedrapidlynorthwardto25°–30°Nlatitude(Figures12b
and13b),withtheNCBtravelingmorerapidlynorthwardthantheXSB(Figure12b),therebyreducingthe
differenceinpaleolatitudebetweenthetwoblocks.Meanwhile,therewasarelativerotationof~20°between
them(TableS2;Figure12c)thatmainlyresultedfromthecontinuousclockwiserotation(~19.8°)oftheNCB
(Figure12c)andaminoranticlockwiserotation(~0.6°)oftheXSB.Theseplatemovementsculminatedin

thewesternpartoftheNCBcollidingwiththeXSB,andtheresultingclosureofthewesternPAOcreateda
smallwedge‐shapedoceanbasin(Figure13b).ThedistributionoftheMiddle–LatePermiansyncollisionalor
postcollisionalgranitesinthewesternsuturezone(Eizenhöfer&Zhao,2018;Wangetal.,2017)supportsour
conclusionthatthewesternpartsofthetwoblockswereconnectedatthistime.Furthermore,theformation
oftheMiddle–LatePermianophioliticmélangesintheeasternpartofthePAO,suchastheSolonkerophio-
litic mélange (~268–260 Ma; Fu et al., 2018) and the Late Permian ophiolitic mélanges in the
Changchun‐Yanjiarea(Liuetal.,2019,2017andreferencestherein),indicatesthatanoceanbasinexisted
in the region during the Middle–Late Permian. The Angara flora of the Boreal realm began to mix with
the Cathaysia Flora, including such typical Cathaysia Flora as Glossopteris sp. cf. G. communis
Feistmantel,whichhasbeendiscoveredinlateMiddlePermianstratainthewesternXSB(Naugolnykh&
Uranbileg,2018).Inaddition,thepaleoclimategraduallybecamearidinthewesternpartsofthetwoblocks
(e.g., Helanshan Region, northwestern China; Sun & Deng, 2003), and the Zhesi brachiopods (Wang &
Zhang,2003)ineasternpartsgraduallybecameextinctduringtheMiddle–LatePermianduetothenarrow-
ingofthePAObasin(Figure13a–b).
Inourtectonicreconstruction,theLaurussiaandSiberiadomainsunderwentnosignificantplatemovement
duringtheMiddle–LatePermian(Figure13);however,theEastAsianblocksandsomeblocksassociated
withtheTethysdomain(e.g.,NorthQiangtangTerraneandtheIndochinaBlock)movednorthwardwith
tectonic rotations from ~265 to 255 Ma (Figures 13b and 13c). The rapid movement of these blocks was
accompanied by the rapid and extensive subduction of Paleo‐Asian, Mongol–Okhotsk, and Paleo‐Tethys
oceaniclithosphereduringtheMiddle–LatePermian(Figure13b;Eizenhöfer&Zhao,2018;Chenetal.,2020;
Collins,2003;Heetal.,2014;Zorin,1999),asevidencedbyanincreasedabundanceofarcmagmaticrocks,
pyroclastics,andignimbritesatthecontinentalmarginoftheEastAsiandomain(e.g.,NCBandSCB),the
NorthQiangtangTerrane,andtheIndochinaBlock(Heetal.,2014;Soreghanetal.,2019).
Inadditiontoaglobaleventat~251Ma(theend‐Permianmassextinction;Stanley&Yang,1994),amass
extinction event of marine benthic organisms occurred at the end‐Guadalupian (Shen & Shi, 2002), the
effectsofwhichwereprobablymoststronglyfeltatthecommunitylevel(e.g.,EastAsia)andweretaxono-
micallyselective(epibenthos,e.g.,brachiopods,fusulinids,andcorals;Chen&Xu,2019;Shen&Shi,2002).
This might have been the effect of global paleoclimatic and sea‐level change (Shen, Zhang, et al., 2019;
Sun,1999,2006)andvoluminousvolcanicactivity(e.g.,~260‐MaEmeishanvolcanism;Figure13b;Chen
&Xu,2019;Soreghanetal.,2019).Thetrendofincreasedregionalextinctionawayfromthetropicshasbeen
identifiedthroughthecompilingofmarinegenerafromend‐PermianfossiloccurrencesinthePaleobiology
Database(Pennetal.,2018).Inthispaper,ourobservationsthatEastAsianblocksdriftedrapidlynorthward
to25°–30°Nfrom~265to255Ma(Figure12b)andthatthegradualclosureofthePAOoccurredoverthat
time suggest that plate tectonics was an important factor in the extinction event (e.g., Zhesi brachiopod
fauna in the Boreal Realm). This led to both sides of the SLS rapidly transforming from a Middle–Late
Permian humid environment to a more arid setting in the Early–Middle Triassic (Heumann et al., 2012;
Johnsonetal.,2008),probablyacceleratingamassextinctioneventintheEastAsianblocks.
During~255–246Ma,theXSBandNCBremainedat20°–30°N(Figures12band13c)butcontinuedtheir
relativerotation,whichcreateda“trafficjameffect.”Aleft‐lateralstrike‐stripfaultalongthewestsegment
oftheSLSaccommodatedtherelativemovementbetweentheNCBandXSB,resultinginaregionaldefor-
mation event (Natal'in & Şengör, 2005). The XSB experienced negligible clockwise rotation during
255–248 Ma but the NCB underwent continuous counterclockwise rotation of ~12.7° with some
right‐lateraltranslationduring255–246Ma.Themovementof the NCBwassignificant duringthistime,
completing the collision between the NCBand the XSB (Figure13c). The dynamic mechanismthat pro-
ducedthisrotationoftheNCBmayhavebeenthecollisionbetweentheeasternpartsoftheNCBandthe
South China Block (SCB) during the latest Permian to Early Triassic (Figure 13c; Gilder et al., 1999;
Huangetal.,2018;Lietal.,2017).Thescissors‐likeclosureofthePAObasinissupportedbygeologicalobser-
vations,suchasthediachronouscessationoftheformationofsyncollisionalgranitoidsfromwesttoeastdur-
ingtheLatePermiantoEarlyTriassic(Eizenhöfer&Zhao,2018).Becauseofthegradualclosureoftheocean
basin,themigrationandmixingoftheAngaraandCathaysiaflorasoccurredduringtheLatePermian–Early
Triassic(Figure13c;Dengetal.,2009;Sunetal.,2013;Zhangetal.,2014).OurconclusionthattheXSBand
theNCBwereamalgamatedduring~248–246Maissupportedbysimilardetritalzirconagespectrafromthe
latest Permian to earliest Triassic sandstones (Han et al., 2012), the distribution of intermediate‐P/T

### page_21
Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 10.1029/2019JB019114
greenschist–blueschist facies metamorphism, syncollisional S‐type granites, and molasse‐type sediments
duringtheEarlyTriassic(Li,2006;Lietal.,2016,2014;Zhangetal.,2015)andEarlyTriassiccompressive
deformation(e.g.,foldingandthrustingstructures)inEarlyPaleozoicstrata(Lietal.,2016;Tianetal.,2016;
Wangetal.,2013;Xiaoetal.,2018)alongtheSLSzone.
After~248–246Ma,theSLSzonechangedfromintracontinentalcontractiontoapostcollisionalextensional
setting,asevidencedbytheemplacementofA‐typegraniticrocks(Wuetal.,2011)andtheformationofrift
basins(Mengetal.,2018)andmetamorphiccorecomplexes(Davisetal.,2004)duringtheEarly–Middle
Triassic.
9. Conclusions
NewzirconU–PbgeochronologicalandpalaeomagneticresultsfromtheXSBandtheNCBprovideabetter
understandingoftheevolutionoftheSLS,yieldingthefollowingconclusions.
1. We report new geochronological results from the Zhesi Fm tuff beds and Qingfengshan Fm andesite
flows,whichyieldzirconU–Pbagesof266.5±1.8and254.8–257.1Ma,respectively.
2. NewpaleomagneticresultsfromtheZhesiFmredbedspassedafoldtest,andaninclinationshallowing
testandE/Icorrectionhavebeencarriedout.TheresultsfromtheQingfengshanFmandesitesandsand-
stonespassedbothfoldandreversaltests,andPSVintheandesiteshasbeenaveragedout.Twopaleo-
magnetic poles were calculated: for the XSB, the ~265‐Ma pole is at 57.4°N/342.0°E (A = 4.3°); for
95
theNCB,the~255‐Mapoleisat54.3°N/20.2°E(A =3.3°).
95
3. Comparisonofhigh‐qualityPermianpaleomagneticpolesoftheXSBandNCBrevealalatitudinalcon-
vergence and relative rotation between them, leading to a progressive scissors‐like closure of the
Solonker Ocean from west to east between ~265 and ~246 Ma. This controlled the mixing of the
CathaysianandAngaraflorasinspaceandtime.TheXSBandNCBmovedrapidlynorthwardbetween
~265and~255Ma,whichprobablyacceleratedtheend‐GuadalupianmassextinctioninEastAsia.
